guides.title: Check runtime capabilities before choosing a recipe
guides.summary: Use the runtime capability model to distinguish supported transports, required Cloudflare bindings, and process-local behavior before generating or deploying an application.
guides.markdown:
# Plan against the target runtime

Call `describeRuntimeCapabilities(runtime, env)` to inspect the runtime's supported features and the binding names that are missing. It reads binding presence only; never pass binding values to discovery or print them in diagnostics. A supported transport does not imply durable state: Node and Deno can host process-local WebSockets, while durable page state requires Cloudflare Durable Objects. Cloudflare SSE coordination requires `COSSACK_SSE`; Durable Object transport requires `COSSACK_OBJECT`.

For a selected feature set, use `checkCapabilityRequirements` and preserve its structured diagnostics. Do not infer deployed readiness from this static model; deployment credentials, remote bindings, and runtime health are separate checks.

guides.title: Choose cache storage by its consistency and locality
guides.summary: Use the built-in cache facade and inspect provider guarantees so process memory or eventually consistent KV is not used for a cross-instance invariant.
guides.markdown:
# Choose the cache backend by the guarantee you need

The `cache` facade uses milliseconds for TTLs and provides `remember` for cached computations. An in-memory store is local to one process or Worker isolate and is cleared on restart. Cloudflare KV is shared but eventually consistent; it does not provide atomic read-modify-write or bulk prefix deletion. Use a Durable Object or database when correctness needs strong shared consistency, and check declared capabilities before accepting a backend for a required guarantee.

Capability checks describe a configured store. They do not prove that a remote binding is reachable or deployed correctly.

guides.title: Read typed configuration and Worker bindings per request
guides.summary: Use request-scoped config factories for string variables and raw Cloudflare bindings without reading Worker environment state at module load.
guides.markdown:
# Read the active request configuration

Export one default factory from each `src/config/*.ts` file, such as `export default ({ env }) => ({ name: env('APP_NAME', 'Cossack') })`. The framework evaluates these factories for the current request, where Worker bindings are available. Do not read `process.env` or call `env()` at module load.

Use `config('app.name')` for the evaluated config tree. The `cossackConfig()` Vite plugin generates `.cossack/config.d.ts` with inferred factory return types. Include that file in `tsconfig.json` (new scaffold projects do this). Before standalone typechecking, run `cossack config --generate`; use `cossack config --json` to list factory names and type origins without evaluating factories or showing values. Explicit `CossackConfigRegistry` entries override generated shapes for the same key. `env('APP_NAME')` reads a string variable; `binding<D1Database>('DB')` reads a raw binding object. `env()` stringifies objects, so never use it for D1, KV, R2, Email, or Durable Object bindings.

Use `requireEnv()` and `requireBinding()` when a missing value must fail. They throw `ConfigBindingError` with code `COSSACK_BINDING_MISSING`; the diagnostic may list present binding names but never prints their values. In a Worker, declare variables and bindings in each named Wrangler environment because they do not inherit automatically.

Framework middleware establishes the request scope for application code. `prepareConfigStore()` evaluates factories inside a fresh binding scope, so imported required helpers work in factories. `runWithConfig()` enters the completed store for integrations and isolated tests; application pages should read the already-active scope. Outside a scope, `config()` and `env()` return their defaults and `binding()` returns `undefined`.

Export a literal named `requirements` object beside each factory, using `satisfies ConfigRequirements`. Declare variables with `type` (`string`, `number`, `boolean`), optional `coerce`, `required` (defaults to true), `secret`, and `runtimes`. Declare bindings with `kind` (`object`, `d1`, `kv`, `r2`, `durable-object`, `service`), `required`, and `runtimes`. Omitted runtimes apply everywhere, including SSG. SSG supplies APP_URL; live Cloudflare requirements should explicitly use `runtimes: ["cloudflare"]` when static rendering does not need them.

All active requirements validate before the first factory. Read normalized scalars with `requireConfigVariable("PORT", "number")` or optional `configVariable()`; `env()` retains its string behavior. Numeric coercion accepts finite decimal/exponent strings; boolean coercion accepts true/false, 1/0, and their string forms. It rejects yes/no and arbitrary object conversion. Parsed values remain in the server request store. `secret: true` classifies a value; it does not prevent application code from deliberately returning it. Never put secrets into public props or responses.

`cossack config --check --env staging --json` checks static literals against selected Wrangler declarations. It does not execute factories, read .env/process values, or contact remote resources. Secret existence remains unverified. Node/Deno declaration checks are explicitly unavailable; request validation still supports those runtimes. Dynamic, mutated, imported or otherwise ambiguous metadata is unknown, not evaluated. `cossack deploy` and `cossack check cloudflare` perform the same check before tools run. Direct Vite builds with cossackConfig() perform the same Cloudflare declaration check before type generation and build output. Select runtime/environment explicitly with cossackConfig({ runtime, environment }); otherwise project metadata and CLOUDFLARE_ENV select them. Each build rechecks source and Wrangler declarations. Node/Deno builds check static metadata and runtime compatibility only; supplied values remain unverified. Development startup permits incomplete values so you can configure the app.

guides.title: Persist fenced job claims in a D1 ledger
guides.summary: Persist fenced job claims in a D1 ledger.
guides.markdown:
createD1JobStore accepts a narrow structural JobStateDatabase binding. Apply jobStateSchema explicitly through setup/migrations, then use the durable store with the core Cloudflare job runtime. The jobs scaffold feature provisions JOBS producer/consumer configuration and independent JOB_STATE D1 binding/migration without requiring the ORM. Node/Deno scaffold targets reject Cloudflare jobs before writing. Bind resources separately for each deployment environment and await Worker queue consumption.

Atomic claim increments the persisted logical attempt, not the provider delivery counter. Token-fenced complete/fail reject old owners. Retry deadlines survive fresh connections/store instances, and terminal keys remain deduplicated until your retention policy deletes them. inspect reads bounded structural state without setup writes or payloads/secrets. D1 SQL/transport errors must not be exposed as public diagnostics.

This executable example uses the public adapter over an actual file-backed Node SQLite structural binding. It proves restart/backoff/fencing semantics locally; it does not establish remote D1 permissions or throughput. Deploy the same schema through Wrangler D1 migrations and run local workerd/selected-environment acceptance separately. A durable claim ledger cannot alone guarantee exactly-once external effects; use transactional receipts/provider idempotency and design lease duration for handler execution. See repository docs/jobs.md.

guides.title: Use explicit email providers and a durable notification ledger
guides.summary: Use explicit email providers and a durable notification ledger.
guides.markdown:
createCloudflareNotificationEmailProvider accepts the current structured send_email binding subset (to/from/subject/html/text). Supply Wrangler-generated application binding types, private configuration, selected-environment resources and an onboarded sender domain. It declares idempotency:none and maps documented explicit rejection to fixed errors; unknown/internal failure remains uncertain. A resolved send returns provider-accepted only. The adapter never automatically retries or echoes bodies/raw exceptions.

createD1NotificationStore uses a narrow structural D1 interface and notificationStateSchema applied through explicit migration. No ORM dependency is needed. Generated notifications can share JOB_STATE with jobs while applying their additional schema. State contains private rendered content/data/recipient addresses; database permissions and retention belong to the application. Runtime inspection is structural; internal store.get is not an authorized browser endpoint.

Atomic claims, unexpired token fences and a persisted pre-send marker prevent blind resend after uncertain non-idempotent delivery. Terminal acceptance/unknown survives restart. Provider-enforced idempotency permits recovery with the same key; a capability downgrade is blocked. Store-owned attempts and exact tenant/user inbox/read filters remain authoritative. Reads never create schema. Local SQLite structural tests and local workerd fixtures do not prove authenticated remote acceptance. See docs/notification-providers.md. The example performs actual SQLite restart with an injected binding and sends no email.

guides.title: Compose server R2 and S3 providers
guides.summary: Use Storage around either cloud provider. Derive tenant context from authentication and object keys from server rules. Raw providers do not apply authorization. Both providers implement streamed CRUD with metadata and fixed redacted failures; remote deployment credentials and service reachability require actual provider acceptance.
guides.markdown:
Use Storage around either cloud provider. Derive tenant context from authentication and object keys from server rules. Raw providers do not apply authorization. Both providers implement streamed CRUD with metadata and fixed redacted failures; remote deployment credentials and service reachability require actual provider acceptance.

Inject an R2 binding per request. Create the S3Client in server-only configuration with private credentials or a runtime credential provider. Never publish access keys in Worker vars or client state. Signed Storage URLs target an application endpoint served by handleSignedRequest; redemption checks expiry, upload constraints, signature, and authorization again. They are not provider URLs or direct bucket credentials. Set a secret of at least 32 bytes and use HTTPS outside local loopback.

These factories accept typed real provider dependencies and do not create fake cloud bindings. Call them from server handlers. The guide does not run a remote upload during discovery.

guides.title: Use workflow bindings through the pure provider entry
guides.summary: Import workflows/provider for server APIs and Node SSG module loading. This entry has no cloudflare:workers import. The native workflows entry must stay in the Worker export graph. Define schemas for input and events, stable versioned names, explicit tenant/actor scope, and authorization for invoke/inspect/event/control.

guides.title: Compose request-scoped persistent sessions
guides.summary: Register createSessionMiddleware after your per-request store factory and before application handlers. Supply the ORM-agnostic SessionStore contract; the framework does not create a database. session() reads the active framework request context, so call it inside request code only.
guides.markdown:
Register createSessionMiddleware after your per-request store factory and before application handlers. Supply the ORM-agnostic SessionStore contract; the framework does not create a database. session() reads the active framework request context, so call it inside request code only.

Unknown cookie IDs receive a server-created session. bindUser rotates anonymous identity and destroys the old session; auth-managed rotation belongs to the auth provider. TTLs are milliseconds. A store must preserve unrelated concurrent key writes and define persistence and expiry. Set or destroy cookies before headers become immutable, including streamed response headers. Never use client-supplied session contents as authorization.

The factory example constructs middleware without performing I/O. Existing session concurrency and installed database acceptance prove real store behavior.

guides.title: Plan typed routes and read-only rendering tooling
guides.summary: Use filesystem route IDs for component/service ownership. Generated route contracts and defineApi schemas establish typed input/output; runtime parsing and authorization still run at the boundary. Numeric IDs are build artifacts, not durable application identities. Nested layouts retain their browser scope until navigation leaves that owner.
guides.markdown:
Use filesystem route IDs for component/service ownership. Generated route contracts and defineApi schemas establish typed input/output; runtime parsing and authorization still run at the boundary. Numeric IDs are build artifacts, not durable application identities. Nested layouts retain their browser scope until navigation leaves that owner.

Use locale middleware to resolve locale per request. Markdown standard metadata validates before publication, and extension fields require explicit validators. SSG canonical URLs deduplicate sitemap entries while aliases publish the same canonical page. Resolve output collisions before writing static assets. Browser code comes from the security compiler, not a runtime permission check.

Vite plugins own route/config/SSG generation. Use cossack inspect/check and the build/deployment artifact tooling to inspect declared requirements and provenance without importing application modules or printing environment values. Build receipts and static capability checks do not prove deployment readiness. Keep Node inspection modules outside browser and Worker bundles. Use client/app only in browser startup and development traces only for development diagnostics. Do not expose state values through traces.

The example combines route resolution, metadata validation, and selected host requirements. It does not build assets or contact Cloudflare.

guides.title: Exercise declared HTTP and class API boundaries
guides.summary: Use defineApi for native Hono handlers with input schemas, output schemas, authorization, finite deadlines and byte limits. Invalid output is a server bug; fixed diagnostics hide provider errors. Native Response handlers preserve response status/headers. Repeated scalar query keys reject unless declared array inputs.
guides.markdown:
Use defineApi for native Hono handlers with input schemas, output schemas, authorization, finite deadlines and byte limits. Invalid output is a server bug; fixed diagnostics hide provider errors. Native Response handlers preserve response status/headers. Repeated scalar query keys reject unless declared array inputs.

A class API route supplies authored get/post methods; createApiHandler provides its request facilities, guarded invocation and cleanup. A class with render also supplies a page, so filesystem routing decides GET HTML versus method dispatch. Use generated contract types for the application API client. A plain fetch client must check response.ok and parse public output; it does not bypass schemas or policies.

This example sends actual Request objects through Hono with the production API handler. It proves typed query input/output and authorization, then verifies a class API handler. Generated app acceptance must additionally verify filesystem discovery and native host signals.

guides.title: Plan and render isolated localized static pages
guides.summary: Collect declared SSG pages, resolve static parameters and render through the same root/hydration pipeline as SSR. Pass explicit public catalogs and render-local configuration. Static rendering has no authenticated user or live provider binding; private route middleware must reject or exclude its output.
guides.markdown:
Collect declared SSG pages, resolve static parameters and render through the same root/hydration pipeline as SSR. Pass explicit public catalogs and render-local configuration. Static rendering has no authenticated user or live provider binding; private route middleware must reject or exclude its output.

createLocaleMiddleware resolves authored content locale ahead of cookie/browser preferences. It loads virtual:cossack-lang from the Vite graph, so direct Node import cannot create its project catalogs. createApp from router similarly consumes generated pages/config/middleware virtual modules; createClientApp requires a browser and the generated pages graph. Keep these entry imports in their respective generated server/client startup, not a standalone Node inspection tool.

In generated startup, import createApp from framework/router for the server and createClientApp from framework/client/app for the browser. Add createLocaleMiddleware from framework/locale to authored URL locale middleware. Those public imports are listed here so discovery detects removed entries. Actual generated Node/workerd/browser acceptance owns this wiring.

The executable example resolves a public site URL from temporary configuration, selects an authored locale with the portable browser-language helper, and plans sitemap URLs. It does not claim to execute SSR. Actual renderSsgPage requires the generated Vite middleware graph; the release SSG acceptance verifies localized render isolation, canonical/alias output and hydration. No private credentials or live provider bindings enter the planning example.

guides.title: Inspect project declarations without evaluating private configuration
guides.summary: Use Node inspection entries to read source declarations before generation or deployment. They parse authored syntax without importing configuration factories or calling application handlers. Dynamic declarations remain unknown rather than guessed. Do not print private variable values, schema literals, factory return values or provider exception details.
guides.markdown:
Use Node inspection entries to read source declarations before generation or deployment. They parse authored syntax without importing configuration factories or calling application handlers. Dynamic declarations remain unknown rather than guessed. Do not print private variable values, schema literals, factory return values or provider exception details.

inspectConfigRequirements reports names, source origins and declared constraints. inspectConfigurationRequirements checks the selected runtime/environment and available Wrangler declaration names, not remote service health. checkConfigBuildRequirements rejects invalid static requirements before output. Page inspection reports authored API/method facts; route IDs and layouts share production routing rules. Keep these filesystem/parser modules outside browser and Worker export graphs.

The example writes a temporary configuration whose factory contains a private sentinel. Inspection must report its requirement without exposing that value or evaluating the factory. It also resolves nested layout ownership from the same route helper used by production. No credentials or remote calls are required.
